To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relic abundance of an exotic particle decaying into neutrinos at a cosmological time scale is constrained to be below about 0.1% of the total energy density of the universe, for a lifetime of about 1 s, if the particle is mostly electrically neutral and has a branching ratio of about 50% into neutrinos and 50% into hadrons.
the relic abundances are constrained by the cosmic microwave background to be smaller than 10^(-5) times the thermal abundance of the lightest neutrino species.

the neutrino injection from a long-lived particle is strongly constrained, with a bound that is typically of order 10-6-10-5, depending on the particle lifetime and the hadronic and electromagnetic decay branching ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question: what can we learn about the cosmological history of the universe if we know that there are neutrinos in it?
The cosmological neutrino background is the most important relic from the early universe.
the following topics: (i) We study the impact of neutrino injection on the primordial deuterium abundance.
the cosmological consequences of a hypothetical long-lived particle which may decay into neutrinos.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no room for long-lived particles decaying into neutrinos at cosmological time-scales.
the neutrino injection from the decay of an exotic particle is severely constrained, and that the most stringent bounds are obtained from the diffuse neutrino and gamma-ray fluxes.
the cosmological constraints are not very strong.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a long-lived particle with lifetime of 0.1–10 s and electromagnetic and hadronic decay branching ratios of 10–100% can be excluded if the neutrino is a massless sterile neutrino.
the relic density of such a particle is constrained to be less than 0.01% of the critical density, unless the lifetime is less than 1 s or the branching ratios are very small.

, if the lifetime is shorter than about a second, the constraints are mainly from the diffuse neutrino and gamma ray fluxes, and if the lifetime is longer than about a second but shorter than about 10^4 s, the constraints are from the cosmic microwave background.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for lifetimes longer than about 10^4 sec, the constraints on the neutrino injection from the cosmic microwave background become more stringent than the ones from the diffuse photon and neutrino fluxes, and the big bang nucleosynethsis bounds are not relevant.
a large class of models can be constrained by the diffuse neutrino flux.

, for a long-lived particle decaying into a neutrino with a lifetime of order a few seconds, a branching ratio of order a few percent into electromagnetic and a branching ratio of less than a few percent into hadrons is required.
